(2) The derived deadlock_freedom obligation over Operate substates is undermined because the exact named substates Idle, Accelerating, Braking are structurally present but unreachable from the region's own local initial edges (AccelerateRegion's local initial routes to CruisingState only under a guard, and to UnspecifiedInitial unconditionally, never to AcceleratingState; IdleRegion's local initial never reaches IdleState; BrakeRegion's local initial never reaches BrakingState), so ongoing substate transition among the named substates cannot occur as continuously as NL3 requires. (4) The endpoint contracts NL2-ENDPOINT-1 and NL2-ENDPOINT-2 are satisfied at the exact required scope (OffState<->OperateState) so are omitted from candidates by this lens. I derive one additional contract capturing the exact reachability defect for the named operating substates that NL1/NL3 designate as the actual behavioral loci of Operate, since the supplied contracts only cover Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking containment, not their reachability, and cross-view facts (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics, verify_facts refuted reachability checks) reveal this causal reachability gap that NL-only extraction could not see.

But the exact guard facts also show the inter-region transitions (line:47 guard==4, line:48 guard==5, line:49/50/51 guard==6/7/8) carry mutually exclusive route-token values, meaning at the region level the alternatives are technically guard-disjoint and do not collide at runtime. This is a genuine rebutting reading supported by the exact guard facts: the property under review (guard_disjointness) is satisfied by the region-level guards even though the depth/naming does not match NL1's leaf-level vocabulary, so the rebuttal survives rather than being defeated, leaving only a naming/depth-mismatch concern rather than a proven guard-collision violation.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The IdleRegion/AccelerateRegion/BrakeRegion transitions carry mutually exclusive route-token guards (4 and 5 for the Idle-sourced pair; 6/7/8 for the Accelerate-sourced set), so at the region level -- the level at which the guard_disjointness property is actually evaluated -- the alternatives remain guard-disjoint; the mismatch is a naming/depth difference between NL's leaf-state vocabulary and the model's region-level structure, not a runtime guard collision.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL1's four named substates (Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking) must form one set of mutually exclusive, directly user-selectable alternatives from a shared Operate source, matching the transition-group's guard-disjointness structure.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers keyOff row (consumer_state_refs vs reachable_consumer_state_refs); exact transition fact at line:59 (OperateState->OffState, guard R45RouteToken==10); NL1 and NL2 quotes on operating substates and keyOff turn-off
decisions.reason: The exact event_consumers fact for keyOff confirms IdleState/AcceleratingState/BrakingState are declared consumers but excluded from reachable_consumer_state_refs, establishing that the three named substates cannot themselves consume keyOff. Nonetheless, the exact model also supplies a root-level OperateState -> OffState transition (transition:line:59, guard R45RouteToken==10) that is reachable and provides a coarser exit path for the Operate composite as a whole once any reachable leaf (e.g., an UnspecifiedInitial placeholder or CruisingState) processes keyOff. This is an exact, supplied fact -- not a conceivable hypothetical -- that supports a competent alternative reading under which the coarser 'Operate scope can exit via keyOff' obligation is satisfied even though the three named leaf substates individually cannot consume it. Because this alternative is grounded in an exact transition fact rather than a bare possibility, it survives as a rebuttal to the strict per-named-substate reading, while the narrower named-substate gap remains a genuine, separately tracked concern.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The root-level OperateState -> OffState transition (transition:line:59, guard R45RouteToken==10) is reachable and provides a keyOff-driven exit for the Operate composite as a whole once any reachable leaf state processes keyOff, so the system can still be turned off during Operate even though IdleState, AcceleratingState, and BrakingState cannot individually consume keyOff.
decisions.violated_obligation: keyOff must be reachably consumable by the Operate substates NL2 describes (Idle, Accelerating, Cruising, Braking) so the system can be turned off from any operating substate.

issues.reason: The transition group asserts one shared source (Operate) with four exclusive alternatives sharing a common 'based on user actions' guard. This mismatch between the NL's flat mutually-exclusive framing and the model's actual nested/guarded topology is a structural guard-distinguishability concern that has no direct frozen predicate expression, so it is preserved as predicate-null W1 per protocol for guard_disjointness claims.

I derive one additional contract capturing the exact reachability defect for the named operating substates that NL1/NL3 designate as the actual behavioral loci of Operate, since the supplied contracts only cover Idle/Accelerating/Cruising/Braking containment, not their reachability, and cross-view facts (STATE_UNREACHABLE_FROM_INITIAL diagnostics, verify_facts refuted reachability checks) reveal this causal reachability gap that NL-only extraction could not see. The named leaf targets IdleState/AcceleratingState/BrakingState are further unreachable from initial entry, so the only actually reachable representatives of each named alternative are synthetic UnspecifiedInitial placeholders (for Idle/Accelerating/Braking) and CruisingState, none of which is disjointly selected by a single user action from one shared Operate-level guard/trigger set as the NL group implies.
candidate.reason: The transition group asserts one shared source (Operate) with four exclusive alternatives sharing a common 'based on user actions' guard. Grounding the exact model shows the actual selection structure is a three-level hierarchy (regions containing named leaf states, connected internally by route-token-guarded synthetic transitions) rather than one flat exclusive-alternative set, and Cruising is not a sibling alternative at all but a nested descendant of the Accelerating branch. This mismatch between the NL's flat mutually-exclusive framing and the model's actual nested/guarded topology is a structural guard-distinguishability concern that has no direct frozen predicate expression, so it is preserved as predicate-null W1 per protocol for guard_disjointness claims.
